theme.title: Rotation: Growth → Value & Defensives
theme.summary: Utilities (-0.80%) and Consumer Staples (-0.92%) led the market today, while Technology (-7.87%) and Industrials (-4.18%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -4.48% versus -1.41% for defensives and -2.93% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. That shows up at the index level too: the blue-chip Dow gained -3.44% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell -5.54%, a wide enough gap to matter. Small caps moved roughly in line with the broader market, with the Russell 2000 at -4.45%. The VIX rose 70.07% to 28.18, pointing to a bit more caution creeping in beneath the surface. Gold slipped 1.21% to $4,099.40, crude oil was little changed at $91.28, and bitcoin gained 0.45% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
